title: introduce-attribute-hashproof-rbac-compactifier-and-kms-context-preserver
author: Nora Chen
description:
Motivation: Large, denormalized RBAC policy blobs and verbose audit payloads were inflating the policy store and audit ingress costs for high-scale tenants. This PR adds a compactifier for RBAC v2 policy payloads plus an attribute-hashproof layer that canonicalizes operator/service attributes into a stable fingerprint. The PR also preserves and forwards KMS context tags (kms:region, kms:origin, kms:tenant-hash) through policy transformations so downstream components (audit ingesters and kms-proxies) can rehydrate provenance information without adding fields to the canonical policy schema.

What this PR does (high level):
- policy/compiler/compactifier: new compact serialization that collapses repeated role/claim references and tokenizes attribute keys to reduce stored size (~35% median reduction in synthetic tests).
- rbac/denormalizer: reversible denormalizer so the compactified policies can be expanded for explainability endpoints. Denormalizer guarantees semantic equivalence and includes ops-safe asserts.
- attribute/hashproof: deterministic attribute fingerprinting using HKDF-SHA256 over normalized attribute tuples; fingerprints are stable across policy rollouts and safe for indexing/search. Hash output is namespaced (attrpf:v1).
- kms/context_preserve: plumbing to extract and persist KMS context tags from incoming requests into policy metadata (not surface-visible in APIs) so audit writers and KMS proxies can attach provenance without schema churn. Context tags are encrypted at rest when stored in policy store.
- audit/anchor: audit anchor writer uses the attribute fingerprint to attach an anchor id to audit events, enabling server-side dedup and compact retention strategies.

Backward compatibility and safety notes:
- Compactifier is additive and opt-in: existing policies remain unchanged unless a migration job runs. The denormalizer allows on-the-fly expansion for older consumers.
- Attribute fingerprints are collision-resistant but not reversible; we intentionally do not derive PII from the fingerprinted data.
- KMS context preservation is gated behind a feature flag (rbac.compactifier.kms_context_forward) and an enterprise tenant guard.

Review conversation (high level):
- Evan Liu: "Nice approach. Two asks: (1) add a short-circuit path for policies < 1KB to skip compaction; (2) what is the expected CPU cost on control-plane jobs?"
- Nora Chen (author): "Addressed (1) in compactifier.go — tiny policy fast-path added. For (2) synthetic bench: median CPU cost +12% on a single worker for compaction; migration should be run during off-peak windows. Added bench results to the doc."
- Priya Desai: "Ensure encryption keys for KMS context are tenant-scoped and rotateable. Also prove the fingerprinting doesn't leak operator emails."
- Nora Chen: "Implemented tenant-scoped KMS envelope and added tests. Fingerprinting normalizes and redacts email-like patterns before hashing; added unit tests to validate non-reversibility."
- Marco Alvarez: "Audit anchor schema looks good; consider TTL-based dedupe instead of absolute anchors for high-cardinality workloads."
- Nora Chen: "Good call — added anchor TTL option and configured default TTL to 24h in anchor writer. Documented operational tradeoffs."
